item.stance: Dave's dread has become a kind of courteous acquaintance; he speaks to the cold, apologizes at Mary Ellery's grave, and the woman appears visibly, greets him, and fades, leaving him grateful rather than afraid.

citedSentences.text: It started on a wet Tuesday, when the pocket of cold had been particularly bad, standing in the middle of the runner so that he had to walk around it to reach the stairs, and Dave was carrying a laundry basket and his arms were full and he was tired of it in a plain, uncomplicated way.
“Look,” he said to the hall at large.
“I don’t know what you are.
But the cold’s in my way and it’s making a draught in the front room.
Would you mind?”
The cold went out of the hall.

It thinned the way frost does under a warm hand — a little at the edges, then all of it, so that when he walked the runner to the stairs with his basket the air was merely an old house’s air, cool and still and entirely ordinary.
“You’re being polite,” he said to the hallway, half-mocking, half not.
But it had gone warm-ish, and it stayed warm-ish, and Dave found that warmth somehow more difficult to bear than the cold had been.
“I’m sorry about the house,” he said, and felt foolish, and went on, because there was nobody to hear.
“If it means anything.
I don’t think I’ve been courteous about it.”
That night he came up the stairs slowly with the lamp brown above his head, and on the landing she was waiting.
“Hello,” he said.
“You said it was in your way,” she said.
“It was.”
“No.”
She inclined her head.
It was slower than that, and older, the way a woman is courteous at a doorway to someone who has come a long way.
Dave felt the greeting land in his chest like a hand laid flat.
“I’m Dave,” he said, stupidly.
“I know.”
“Thank you,” he said, too late, at the empty landing, at the yellowish lamp.
It smelled of dry lavender, faint, in a drawer too long shut.

A door I had not noticed opened onto a corridor with better lighting and worse carpet.
I walked out of the thread.

item.subject: place:halvern
item.object: Infected kneel at a hole in the brewhouse fence and drink spilled wort with their mouths in the mud, making the sound of men drinking something they need.

citedSentences.text: There is a place at the base of the brewhouse fence where a pallet had rotted and the drain from the brewhouse ran out under it.
It had run under the fence and made a small dark patch in the dirt, and three of the infected were kneeling in it.
Kneeling with their faces down in the mud, hands flat, like men at prayer.
One of them had its mouth open and its throat working, and it was making a sound I'd heard a hundred times before and never once from a dead throat.
It was the sound of a man drinking something he needed.

item.subject: place:rift
item.object: The team killed Renekton, Lee Sin and Blitzcrank, then took river control and warded the Baron pit and the enemy jungle mouth.

citedSentences.text: He died mid-stun.
He kicked me into the wall, which was the only thing he had time for, and then he was dead and I was standing in the river with a shutdown’s worth of gold and my ult at forty.
“I’m going to die,” Ilya said, “but I’m going to die with my hook up,” and then Bo shot Blitzcrank in the face and Blitzcrank died before he could press a button.
We took it.
We warded the pit and the mouth of their jungle, and for the first time in the game the dark belonged to us.

item.subject: char:gideon
item.object: Gideon's co-op raid set out eleven strong and returned ten; Pell was killed after an infected seized his wrist under the tarp, and Marisol put him down at the edge of the lane.

citedSentences.text: Eleven of us.
Something under it got his wrist with the whole of its weight behind it.

She put the rifle barrel in the tarp and fired, once, and the tarp stopped moving, and then she stood looking down at Pell's wrist and the blood going out of it in that slow way that means the wound is deep and quick.

Marisol put him down at the edge of the lane, under the load, and did not let the others watch, and then she came back with her knife wet and wiped it on the grass three times, and nobody said anything at all, and the silence went on long enough to be its own sack of malt.
Eleven went out and ten came back and the ten were bringing four hundred pounds of malt and a starter that would be raising wort by nightfall.

item.object: The respirator issued to Nadia is stamped with the word 'reversion'.
